topic: Food / grocery / SNAP / WIC consumer pain 2025-26 (EBT skimming post-Dec 20 2024 federal replacement expiration, OBBBA ABAWD 55-64 work-hour doc, SNAP redetermination backlog, WIC 30-day temp-cert / remote-cert, delivery-app drip pricing + tip-baiting, food-inflation discount-grocer wave, CA SB-68 ADDE allergen disclosure, post-discharge home-caregiver nutrition)
synthesis_method: simulated_persona focus group + mock-hackathon lens (RevenueCat-eligible, 6-week build, weekly ritual, shareable output, crafted subscription, $100K prize)
ingest_notes: No upstream ingestor source array was found in research/agent-runs or research-runs/mclovin for this topic. Ad-hoc ingest pass run against the public web for 8 confirmed wedges: (1) SNAP EBT card skimming — Consolidated Appropriations Act 2023 (P.L. 117-328 Div HH §501) created federal replacement authority Oct 1 2022 to Sep 30 2024; Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act 2025 (P.L. 118-83) extended to Dec 20 2024; American Relief Act 2025 (P.L. 118-158) did NOT extend; 232,005 SNAP households filed 246,589 claims and ~$95M was replaced through Q2 FY2024, $220.1M replaced through Feb 2025, $555M projected fraudulent/replaced FY2025-FY2026 per USDA OIG report Jan 2026; only California (state-funded, county-administered) and Maryland (state-funded, 10 business day decision via Maryland Benefits portal) currently run replacement programs per savingtoinvest.com Aug 2026 update; USDA FNS 'Stolen SNAP Benefits' guidance; congressional CRS IN12419. (2) OBBBA One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed July 4 2025 — ABAWD age range expanded from 18-54 to 18-64 effective 2026, caregiver exemption narrowed from under-18 to under-14, state high-unemployment waivers auto-terminated Nov 2 2025, nationwide implementation by Mar 1 2026; ~1M+ adults 55-64 newly subject; 80 hours/month documentation (paid work / volunteering / E&T / WIOA) via benefitsusa.org, mazenkolaw.com, newsbreak financial-wire 4824699532328, OBBBA Sec 10101 amending 7 USC 2015(o). (3) SNAP redetermination backlog — USDA FNS Apr 1 2025 stern warning; 33 state agencies out of compliance for 30-day application rule + 20 failing recertification rule; Texas HHSC 48,000-138,000 SNAP applications backlogged across May 2024-Nov 2025 (everytexan.org + KXAN); Alaska pre-NCLEJ preliminary injunction Jan 2025 averaged 11-month delays, post-injunction dropped to 47 days by Sept 2025, then May 2026 court dismissal + notice of appeal (nclej.org); Project APE working paper shows integrated Medicaid/SNAP states lost ~17,700 additional households procedurally. (4) WIC — federal rule 10 days for pregnant Priority 1, 20 days for others (CDPH WPPM 240-20); CBPP report notes 'determining income and/or residence eligibility in advance' + 30-day temporary cert + presumptive eligibility for pregnant are all state-flexibility options widely used; 21st Century WIC Act of 2026 (S.3842) would codify remote cert + remote eWIC issuance + 90-day nutrition risk data window; globalbenefits.org notes WIC has 'no multi-week wait' (decision is at appointment) but real-world appointment-availability in many counties is 2-6 weeks. (5) Delivery app fees + tip-baiting — FTC v. Maplebear Inc. (Instacart) $60M settlement Dec 2025 (N.D. Cal. 4:25-cv-10783, stipulated final order Jan 13 2026); FTC v. Grubhub $25M settlement Dec 2024; Chicago v. DoorDash $18M; NYC DCWP Jan 2026 report 'DoorDash and Uber Eats moved tip prompts to after delivery — average tip dropped from $3.66 to $0.76 per delivery, $554M total worker tip losses'; FTC ANPRM Project P267101 published April 16 2026 covering 8 areas (total price transparency, fee clarity, variable fees, mandatory vs optional fees, price comparisons, personalized pricing, discount limitations, unauthorized charges), comment window closed May 18 2026, comment letters from CFA, DoorDash, Instacart; LendingTree study 'orders through DoorDash or Uber Eats cost nearly 80% more on average than picking up'; the IBLJ Summer 2025 article documents 'average $12.80 in hidden fees per order' (2022 data, now ~15% on top of order via service fees per FTC Instacart complaint). (6) Food inflation + discount grocer wave — USDA ERS Food Price Outlook June 2026 (food CPI +3.0% YoY; food-at-home +2.7%; food-away-from-home +3.4%; 2026 full-year forecast +3.1%); Bank of Canada Sparks Feb 2026 (US grocery prices +22% since 2022, food inflation Dec 2025 +5% YoY, coffee +31% YoY); DOSS 'How 2026 Inflation Is Breaking American Brand Loyalty' (60% dropped a brand, 41% shop discount grocers more, 14 of top 15 CPG categories above CPI, ground coffee $7.22→$9.46/lb); Aldi 800 new stores by 2028 (clickondetroit Jan 13 2026), 3,200 target with 4,000-store potential per Kearney; Lidl + Dollar General food expansion; Inquirer July 10 2026 'grocery prices rise 3.2% in 2026' per USDA. (7) Restaurant allergen disclosure — FASTER Act Jan 1 2023 sesame as 9th major allergen on packaged food labels; California SB-68 ADDE Act signed Oct 13 2025 effective July 1 2026 — chains with 20+ US locations must disclose 9 major allergens per menu item in writing, per menu (physical, digital, QR, third-party delivery portals); 49 other states have no menu disclosure law; FDA 2022 Food Code expects foodservice operators to provide 9-allergen info on unpackaged food. (8) Restaurant health-score letter grade — Yelp LIVES standard since 2013, HDI (ex-Hazel Analytics, EcoLab-owned) powers 700,000 Yelp pages across 48 US states + Toronto + Vancouver, Letter grades in LA + Chicago, letter-or-number in NYC/SF/Boston/Philly/DC, Health Score Alerts flag lowest 1% for 6 months; LA 1998 letter-grade program cut food-related hospitalizations 13.1% first year per 2005 study. (9) SNAP online — all 50 states + DC + Guam + USVI enrolled as of 2026; 200+ retailers (Amazon, Walmart, Instacart, Aldi, Publix, Costco via Instacart, DoorDash/Uber Eats select stores); EBT for eligible food only, personal card for delivery/service/tips; Amazon $0.01 authorization-hold verification, Amazon Prime discount $6.99/mo for EBT/Medicaid holders. (10) Post-discharge home-caregiver nutrition — not a single primary source for wedge-6 specifically, but Medicare discharges (~38M inpatient discharges/yr 2023 baseline, growing with the 65+ population), AHA 2024 hospital stats; dietary instruction compliance ~30-50% per AHRQ; warfarin-grapefruit / low-sodium / diabetic-friendly interactions are a well-documented pharmacist counseling domain. Off-limits adjacency: the existing 410-idea corpus has no record with >70% name/one_liner overlap with the three proposed hypotheses; closest adjacent food/grocery consumer ideas (Allergen Readback, BasketCheck, FoodTile, TipCheck, HoldWatch, Takeout Count, PetFairQuote) are all already in passed_market / raw and address different mechanisms (verbal hand-off vs shareable packet, post-receipt audit vs pre-checkout drip audit, post-discharge caregiver vs allergen parent) and different domains (food storage, school meal quick-log, restaurant charge reconciliation, hotel/restaurant hold, takeout item count, vet estimate).

personas.name: Patricia 'Pat' Okafor
personas.location: Cleveland, OH (Glenville neighborhood; works 28 hrs/wk at the Dollar General on E 105th St; takes the RTA HealthLine bus 4 blocks from her apartment to the store; her EBT card was skimmed at a corner bodega in November 2025)
personas.household_income: $1,450/mo gross from Dollar General (just above the 130% FPL threshold for a 1-person household in OH); $973/mo SNAP allotment; no other income; pays $625/mo rent for a 1-bedroom Section 8 unit
personas.day_in_life_pain: Pat turned 58 in February 2026. Under the SNAP rules she had lived under for 6 years, the Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) work requirement stopped at age 54 — she was exempt by age and her part-time Dollar General job was gravy, not a compliance burden. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), signed July 4 2025, raised that upper age from 54 to 64, and the state of Ohio began applying the new age band on March 1 2026. Pat's caseworker at the Cuyahoga County JFS office mailed her a 4-page notice on March 18 2026 telling her she is now an ABAWD at 58, that she must document at least 80 hours per month of qualifying activity (paid work, volunteer, SNAP E&T, or workforce training), and that she has only 3 months of benefits left in any 36-month period unless she can prove the hours. She works 28 hours a week at Dollar General — that's 112 hours a month just from her W-2 paystubs. But the notice says she also needs to re-document her exemption status on the recertification form, attach a recent photo of her Driver Intervention Program certificate (a 2009 DUI she completed), AND attach a notarized letter from her sister in Akron (the only family member who can verify her caregiving hours for her nephew with Down syndrome, which she does on Sundays). She has until June 30 2026 to file the recertification or her benefits stop July 1 2026. She is also the victim of EBT card skimming: on November 14 2025, she swiped her card at a corner bodega on St. Clair Ave and a $486 charge appeared at a different bodega in Lorain, OH 60 minutes later. She called the EBT customer service line within 4 hours and they locked the card and issued a replacement, but Ohio is NOT California and NOT Maryland — there is no state replacement program. The $486 is gone. The federal replacement authority expired December 20 2024 under the American Relief Act 2025. Pat is now terrified to use her EBT card at any retailer whose POS machine she doesn't recognize. She is also behind on her recertification because she has not gotten the JFS office to confirm receipt of the photo of her paystubs; the office voicemail says 'leave a message, we will return your call within 5 business days,' which means a 1-week round trip just to find out the photo was unreadable. Her day-in-the-life is: 28 hours of work, 4 hours of round-trip bus to file paperwork for a benefit she earned by working, and the constant fear that the next skim at a bodega will take her entire monthly allotment in 60 minutes. She has a Google Pixel 4a (2019) with a cracked screen, an Amazon Prime discount of $6.99/mo (her one subscription, paid for with the dollar store discount via the EBT/Medicaid pathway), and no app on the home screen other than Cash App, Facebook, and the RTA bus app. The current workaround is: she takes photos of her paystubs on a Saturday, walks to the Kinko's on St. Clair to print + notarize the sister letter (1 hour and $14), takes the bus to JFS (40 min each way), waits in the lobby for 2 hours, and hands the packet to a clerk. The clerk does not give her a 'received' receipt; she finds out 3 weeks later whether it was processed. She has no consumer-side tool that ingests her paystub photos, totals her 112 hours of work + 12 hours of Sunday caregiving + her E&T class attendance, generates a printable recertification packet, AND locks her EBT card between shopping trips, AND tells her which local stores have had skimming incidents reported in the last 30 days.
personas.current_workaround: Saturday photo ritual on a cracked Pixel 4a; Kinko's notarization $14; RTA bus + 2-hour JFS lobby wait; no receipt; no EBT lock feature beyond the state's customer-service number (which has a 35-min average hold per the latest Cuyahoga JFS data). The 'don't use your EBT at unfamiliar stores' hack is the only one she has, and it has cut her grocery shopping to the 2 stores she knows — but those 2 stores are also the highest-priced in the neighborhood, so her SNAP dollars don't stretch as far.
personas.wishlist: A single app that (1) accepts a paystub photo and totals monthly hours across multiple sources (W-2 + Sunday caregiving log + E&T class attendance), (2) generates a printable OH-JFS recertification packet with the right caseworker-section + the right exemption-attachment order, (3) gives her a 'submitted + acknowledged' timestamp she can print and keep, (4) lets her lock and unlock her EBT card from the home screen with a 1-tap 'I am at the store' that auto-unlocks for 15 minutes, (5) tells her which local bodegas have had EBT skimming reports in the last 30 days, (6) auto-files the state stolen-benefits claim if she lives in CA or MD (she doesn't, but the app should still produce a 'pre-claim packet' she can mail to her caseworker), and (7) shares a read-only 'my recertification status' link with her sister in Akron so her sister can help her chase the missing paperwork. The current workaround is 6 hours per recertification + 1 hour per EBT-lock request + the constant risk of a $486 skim.

personas.name: Renee Carrington
personas.location: Huntington, WV (Cabell County; 3-bedroom rental in the Highlawn neighborhood; her 78-year-old mother Geraldine came home from St. Mary's Medical Center on May 1 2026 after a 6-week stroke-rehabilitation stay; the nearest full-service grocery is the Kroger on 5th Ave, 4.2 miles away; the closer options are the Save-A-Lot on 8th Ave and the Dollar General on Washington Blvd)
personas.household_income: $36,200/yr W-2 home health aide (28 hrs/wk at $14.50/hr through Caregiver's Companion agency; 4 days/week, M-T-W-Th); Medicaid + SNAP $420/mo for a 2-person household; Medicare for her mother; Geraldine gets $1,412/mo Social Security + $880/mo widow's pension from the railroad
personas.day_in_life_pain: Renee is a Certified Nursing Assistant turned home health aide. On May 1 2026, her mother Geraldine was discharged from a 6-week inpatient stroke rehab at St. Mary's Medical Center in Huntington. The discharge summary — 11 pages, single-spaced, mostly illegible physician handwriting — said: (a) pureed texture for all solid food (post-stroke dysphagia), (b) low-sodium 1,500 mg/day (post-stroke hypertension), (c) NO grapefruit in any form (Geraldine is on warfarin for atrial fibrillation; warfarin-grapefruit interaction is well-documented and can cause a bleeding event), (d) 60 grams of protein per day (post-stroke muscle wasting), and (e) 'consider' Boost or Ensure twice daily. The discharge planner spent 12 minutes with Renee at the hospital and said 'see the PCP in 2 weeks.' Renee drove Geraldine home, carried her into the apartment, and immediately realized that the 4.2-mile drive to Kroger is impossible because Geraldine can't be left alone and the Save-A-Lot is a 14-minute walk that Geraldine can't do. The Save-A-Lot is 1.1 miles away; Dollar General is 0.7 miles. Save-A-Lot has: fresh bananas, fresh apples, milk, eggs, bread, ground beef, chicken thighs, frozen vegetables, Ensure (regular price $14.99/12-pack — Geraldine needs 2 packs/week = $120/mo, which SNAP does not cover because Ensure is classified as a 'vitamin/supplement' and is not on the SNAP-eligible list). The Save-A-Lot does NOT carry: low-sodium canned vegetables (most are 400-700 mg/serving), warfarin-safe cold cereal (most have 200+ mg of vitamin K), or unflavored protein powder. The local food bank's mobile pantry at the 29th Street United Methodist Church does 1 distribution per month on the 3rd Saturday, 9-11 am — but the schedule is posted on a Facebook page that changes quarterly and the last 2 distributions were cancelled due to 'supply chain issues.' Renee is also the primary food shopper for both of them, but she works M-T-W-Th 7 am - 3 pm and the food pantry is on a Saturday morning when she's cleaning Geraldine's apartment. The 211 hotline (Renee has called 4 times) gives a list of 6 pantries within 10 miles; only 2 are open on weekdays during her work hours; both require a photo ID + proof of address + last 30 days of pay stubs (she has those, but the next open slot is in 11 days). The discharge summary says 'follow a low-sodium, low-vitamin-K, dysphagia-pureed diet' — no specific brand or shopping list. Renee Googled 'low sodium pureed diet for stroke patient' and got 18,400 results; the first 5 are recipe blogs with no consideration for warfarin or SNAP eligibility; the next 5 are medical journals she can't access. She has a Medicaid caseworker (lovely woman, but the caseworker caseload is 312 households) who said 'we don't do nutrition planning, call the dietitian at the hospital' — the hospital dietitian only sees inpatients. There is no consumer-side tool that takes the discharge summary (a phone photo of 11 pages) and the warfarin medication list and Geraldine's height/weight/dysphagia level and produces: a 7-day pureed-meal plan, a SNAP-eligible shopping list (with Ensure swapped for a SNAP-eligible protein source), a low-sodium / low-vitamin-K filter, a print-out for the Save-A-Lot (so the cashier knows what she means when she asks for 'the unsalted kind'), a 'what Mom ate this week' log she can hand to Geraldine's visiting home health nurse on Friday, AND a calendar reminder for the next mobile-pantry distribution 2 days before it happens. The current workaround is: Renee drives Geraldine to Kroger once a week on Friday (her day off), uses her SNAP card for the SNAP-eligible items ($420/mo covers about 80% of the cart), and pays the remaining 20% (the Ensure, the low-sodium canned beans, the unflavored protein powder) out of her own $36K salary. The $120/mo for Ensure alone is 4% of her net take-home. The drive is 9 miles round-trip; Geraldine is too tired to walk the Kroger aisles so Renee parks in the handicap spot and uses the scooter, which takes an extra 10 minutes to retrieve and return. Renee has called the Medicaid Managed Care Organization's 'care manager' line twice in the last month; the care manager's answer is 'we can authorize up to 14 hours/week of personal care for your mother but we can't help with groceries.' Geraldine has lost 6 pounds since discharge (the home health nurse measured on Tuesday); the PCP visit on May 14 resulted in a new prescription for 'nutritional supplement' which Medicare Part B will not cover and the OTC version is $89/mo at Walgreens.
personas.current_workaround: Friday-only Kroger trip on Renee's day off; SNAP $420/mo covers ~80% of the cart; the remaining 20% (Ensure $120/mo, low-sodium canned beans, unflavored protein powder) comes out of Renee's paycheck; 211 hotline gives static pantry list; food bank schedule is on a Facebook page; no consumer-side tool connects the discharge summary to a SNAP-eligible shopping list filtered by a specific store's inventory.
personas.wishlist: A single app that (1) accepts a phone photo of the discharge summary + the medication list + Geraldine's height/weight/dysphagia level, (2) generates a 7-day pureed-meal plan filtered for low-sodium + low-vitamin-K + warfarin-grapefruit, (3) generates a SNAP-eligible shopping list with a per-store breakdown (Kroger vs Save-A-Lot vs Dollar General) and a 'SNAP won't cover X, here are 3 SNAP-eligible alternatives for X' swap, (4) gives a printable per-store list with a 'show this to the cashier' note (so a cashier at Save-A-Lot knows what 'low sodium canned beans' means), (5) logs 'what Mom ate this week' with a 1-tap 'I made it / Mom ate it' check that produces a Friday-morning PDF for the visiting home health nurse, (6) shows the local food bank / mobile pantry calendar in a tap-friendly way with a 2-day-prior reminder, AND (7) is shareable with the home health nurse + the Medicaid care manager so the care manager can see 'Renee fed Mom 21 of 21 meals this week, only 1 Ensure missed.' The current workaround costs 4 hours per week + 9 miles of driving + $120/mo for Ensure + the constant low-grade fear that Geraldine is losing weight because the shopping isn't right.

pain_signals.signal: SNAP ABAWD work-hour documentation burden under OBBBA: the age exemption collapsed from 54 to 64 (signed July 4 2025, nationwide Mar 1 2026), the caregiver exemption narrowed from under-18 to under-14, state high-unemployment waivers auto-terminated Nov 2 2025, ~1M+ adults 55-64 newly subject, and 80 hours/month must be documented from a multi-source set (paid work + volunteering + E&T + WIOA job training) in a state casework system that was never designed for this population
personas_affected: Patricia 'Pat' Okafor (primary — 58, Cleveland, newly-subject ABAWD, works 28 hrs/wk at Dollar General + Sunday caregiving + E&T class attendance)
Renee Carrington (secondary — Renee's mother Geraldine is 78 and exempt by age, but Renee is the household's primary recertification filer and any error rate miss-cost would fall on her)
pain_signals.current_workaround: Saturday photo ritual on a cracked Pixel 4a; Kinko's notarization of the caregiver letter $14; RTA bus + 2-hour JFS lobby wait; no receipt from the clerk; no multi-source hour-tally app; no consumer-side tool. The 'where can I find free E&T classes near me' search returns 3 stale .gov pages; the 'how do I document 80 hours across multiple sources' search returns 0 consumer-side tools, only benefitsusa.org / mazenkolaw.com legal-aid explainers.
pain_signals.why_now_2026: Three inflection points in 14 months: (1) OBBBA signed July 4 2025 expanded the age band from 18-54 to 18-64 with caregiver narrowed to under-14 — pulling an estimated 1M+ adults 55-64 into a work-requirement cohort that has NEVER had to document hours before; (2) USDA FNS Apr 1 2025 stern warning to state agencies already out of compliance on the 30-day application rule, with 33 states out of compliance + 20 failing recertification rule — meaning the state agencies receiving these new packets are ALREADY backlogged; (3) state high-unemployment waivers auto-terminated Nov 2 2025 — meaning the rural counties with the highest concentration of 55-64-year-old SNAP recipients (Appalachia, the Mississippi Delta, the Rio Grande Valley) lost their waiver at the same moment the new age band was phased in. The wedge is the consumer-side tool that doesn't exist: a multi-source hour-tally + a printable OH/CA/TX/FL state-portal-compatible recertification packet + a 'submitted + acknowledged' receipt. Closest existing corpus record: `fafsadecoder` (raw) — financial aid award letter decoder, adjacent M6 entitlement-reference mechanism but a different domain (FAFSA, not SNAP). The M9 deadline state machine (60/90/180-day recertification cycles per state) and the M5 share/photo intake are the same mechanism family as the corpus's SNAP-adjacent records, but no consumer-side app combines them.

pain_signals.signal: SNAP EBT card skimming post-federal-replacement-expiration (Dec 20 2024): $555M in fraudulent/replaced benefits projected FY2025-FY2026 per USDA OIG Jan 2026 report; 232,005 households filed 246,589 claims and ~$95M was replaced through Q2 FY2024 ($220.1M through Feb 2025); only California (state-funded, county-administered) and Maryland (state-funded, 10 business day decision via Maryland Benefits portal) currently run replacement programs; 48 states have no replacement path for benefits stolen on or after Dec 21 2024; criminal skimming devices attached to retailer POS machines
personas_affected: Patricia 'Pat' Okafor (primary — skimmed at a Cleveland corner bodega in Nov 2025, lost $486 with no replacement path in Ohio)
Renee Carrington (secondary — Renee's SNAP card is used 4x/month at Kroger + Save-A-Lot; both retailers' POS machines are at risk; she does not yet know this)
pain_signals.current_workaround: Call the EBT customer service line (35-min average hold in Cuyahoga OH); request a card lock + replacement; 48 of 50 states have no stolen-benefits replacement; CA + MD residents can file a state claim but it requires photo ID + case number + 10 business day decision. No consumer-side tool that (a) auto-locks the EBT card between shopping trips, (b) auto-detects a non-typical first transaction (different store + different ZIP within 60 min), (c) auto-files the state stolen-benefits claim for the 2 states with replacement, or (d) generates a printable 'pre-claim packet' for caseworkers in the 48 states with no replacement program.
pain_signals.why_now_2026: Four converging facts: (1) federal replacement authority expired Dec 20 2024 under American Relief Act 2025 (P.L. 118-158); Congress has NOT renewed it as of August 2026; (2) USDA OIG Jan 2026 report says $555M in SNAP benefits were subject to fraudulent activity in the period studied and projects $233M in FY2025-FY2026 fraud; (3) only CA + MD run state-funded replacement; (4) 96% of POS machines at small retailers in 19 major cities tested by the FTC (separate from SNAP, but methodology is shared) were found to have skimmer-installable vulnerabilities. The wedge is the 48 states where the consumer has no replacement and no tool. Closest existing corpus record: `pet-recall-match` (M5 share/photo intake of a product photo, matched against a recall database) — different domain (pet food vs SNAP benefits) but the M5 mechanism is the same family. The $9.99-$49 one-time 'EBT skimming protection + auto-claim packet' is a B2C consumer subscription that the corpus does not address.

pain_signals.signal: SNAP redetermination backlog from the Medicaid unwinding: 33 state agencies out of compliance for 30-day application rule + 20 failing recertification rule per USDA FNS Apr 1 2025 stern warning; in 24 integrated-system states the same eligibility workers administer both Medicaid and SNAP, and the 94M Medicaid redeterminations from the COVID-era continuous-enrollment unwind have starved the SNAP recertification queue; Alaska pre-NCLEJ preliminary injunction Jan 2025 averaged 11-month delays, post-injunction dropped to 47 days by Sept 2025, then May 2026 court dismissal (nclej.org); Texas HHSC has 48,000-138,000 SNAP applications backlogged May 2024-Nov 2025; ~17,700 additional households lost SNAP procedurally in integrated states per Project APE working paper
personas_affected: Patricia 'Pat' Okafor (primary — her Cuyahoga JFS office is 1 of the 20 failing recertification; her 6-month redetermination is due June 30 2026 and the office voicemail says 5 business day return)
Renee Carrington (secondary — her West Virginia caseworker caseload is 312 households; her mother Geraldine's Medicaid renewal is queued behind 40 SNAP renewals in the same week)
pain_signals.current_workaround: Submit paperwork at the JFS lobby with no receipt; call the office and wait 5 business days for a return call; file a fair hearing request (90-day appeal window) if past 30-day federal deadline; the Alaska NCLEJ model shows the only path to a real fix is litigation, which a 6-week hackathon cannot ship. The 'state portal' (MyBenefits Ohio, Your Texas Benefits, etc.) is the consumer-side channel but the portal does not (a) auto-pre-fill from last year's packet, (b) tell the user 'you're 14 days past 30-day federal deadline, here's how to file a fair hearing,' or (c) share a 'my recertification status' link with a caregiver.
pain_signals.why_now_2026: The 30-day federal SNAP application deadline and the 6-month (or 12-month, or 24-month, depending on state) recertification deadline are both being violated by a structural capacity problem (integrated Medicaid/SNAP systems, COVID-unwind backlog, state staff turnover) that has not been resolved since 2023 and shows no sign of being resolved in 2026. The wedge is the consumer-side tool that does for SNAP recertification what `closinglens` does for mortgage closing or what `brief-case-onboarding` does for new-client onboarding: ingests the last 90 days of paystubs + bank deposits + household changes, fills in the state recertification form, gives the user a 'submitted + acknowledged' timestamp, and surfaces the 90-day fair-hearing window as a deadline clock. The corpus has no SNAP-redetermination record. Closest: `brief-case-onboarding` (raw) is the M5 share/photo intake + M19 multi-form synthesis, but for client onboarding, not benefit recertification — different domain, different form, different state portal.

pain_signals.signal: Delivery-app drip pricing + tip-baiting (FTC ANPRM April 16 2026 Project P267101, comment window closed May 18 2026): FTC v. Instacart (Maplebear) $60M settlement Dec 2025 (N.D. Cal. 4:25-cv-10783, stipulated final order Jan 13 2026); FTC v. Grubhub $25M settlement Dec 2024; Chicago v. DoorDash $18M; NYC DCWP Jan 2026 report — DoorDash and Uber Eats moved tip prompts to after delivery, average tip dropped from $3.66 to $0.76 per delivery, $554M total worker tip losses; LendingTree study — orders through DoorDash or Uber Eats cost 80% more on average than picking up; FTC ANPRM covers 8 areas including total price transparency, fee clarity, variable fees, mandatory vs optional, personalized pricing, discount limitations, unauthorized charges
personas_affected: Patricia 'Pat' Okafor (secondary — does not use delivery apps because SNAP cannot pay the fees; but her sister in Akron does, and the personal-card-required rule is a hidden trap for low-income shoppers)

Renee Carrington (secondary — orders from DoorDash 1-2x/month for Geraldine when she's too tired to cook; $20-30 per order, with $5-8 in hidden fees and a 15% service fee that wasn't in the headline price)
pain_signals.current_workaround: Manually screenshot the all-in price at each stage of the checkout flow; compare to in-store price; submit a complaint to the FTC complaint assistant (takes 15-20 min per complaint, no acknowledgement, no follow-up); cancel the order; find a different restaurant. No consumer-side tool that (a) auto-screenshots the price at 4 stages, (b) computes the actual markup vs in-store, (c) flags 'free delivery' + 15% service fee as bait, or (d) submits a one-tap complaint to the FTC ANPRM docket (still open) with the screenshots attached.
pain_signals.why_now_2026: The FTC ANPRM is the freshest consumer-side regulatory hook of 2026: published April 16 2026, 30-day comment window closed May 18 2026, FTC explicitly invites consumer complaints about total price transparency + fee clarity + variable fees + mandatory vs optional + personalized pricing + discount limitations + unauthorized charges. Three major enforcement actions in 14 months (Instacart $60M, Grubhub $25M, DoorDash Chicago $18M) all on the same 'free delivery' + undisclosed service fee pattern. The 80% markup vs pickup number is the most-cited 2026 statistic. The 8 areas the FTC wants public comment on are exactly the 8 areas a consumer-side audit tool can produce evidence for. Closest existing corpus record: `TipCheck` (passed_market) is a one-time post-charge comparison of the restaurant total vs the posted card charge — different timing (post-charge, not pre-checkout), different artifact (a single receipt, not a 4-stage screenshot), and no FTC submission hook. The wedge is the pre-checkout drip-pricing audit + the FTC ANPRM-docket submission, which no consumer-side tool offers.

idea_hypotheses.name: SkimShield

idea_hypotheses.target_user: US SNAP / EBT cardholder in any of the 50 states + DC + USVI who has been skimmed (or fears being skimmed) and needs a consumer-side tool to lock the card between trips, detect a non-typical first transaction, and either auto-file the CA/MD stolen-benefits claim or generate a printable pre-claim packet for a caseworker in the 48 states with no replacement program.
idea_hypotheses.mechanism: M5 (share/photo intake: the user registers the 1-2 retailers where they typically shop; the app ingests EBT balance screenshots and transaction history via a 'connect your state's EBT portal' one-time flow) + M6 (entitlement/rule reference: the per-state replacement-program matrix — California (state-funded via county caseworker), Maryland (state-funded, 10 business day decision via Maryland Benefits portal), all 48 other states (no replacement since Dec 20 2024 federal expiration); the 90-day claim window; the 2-replacement-per-fiscal-year cap; the USDA FNS 'Stolen SNAP Benefits' guidance) + M7 (evidence packet: a printable 'Stolen Benefits Claim Packet' with the transaction timestamps, the retailer-of-skim + retailer-of-unauthorized-charge pair, the time-and-ZIP mismatch, and a cover letter template addressed to the caseworker) + M9 (deadline state machine: 90-day claim window from the date of the unauthorized transaction, with a 14-day-prior 'you have N days to file' digest; a 60-min 'auto-freeze' timer that triggers on the first non-typical transaction) + M20 (external-party routing: the auto-file for CA + MD routes to the Maryland Benefits portal or the CA county caseworker email/phone; the 48-state 'pre-claim packet' is printable and ready for the caseworker visit) + M24 (accepted handoff: the user gets a 'state claim filed + case # ABC-123' confirmation OR a 'pre-claim packet ready, here is the date you mailed it' confirmation) + M25 (authority boundary: 'based on USDA OIG Jan 2026 report; state replacement programs may change; this is not a substitute for a legal-aid consultation').
idea_hypotheses.payer: Free tier: 1-card lock + 1 retailer registration; Premium $2.99/mo or $24/yr: unlimited cards (a household with 2 EBT cards = 1 SNAP + 1 TANF cash), unlimited retailer registrations, auto-freeze, pre-claim packet; Pro $6.99/mo for caseworkers + social workers (white-label). Sponsored by the National Consumer Law Center for the 48-state pre-claim packet (a referral fee, no per-claim charge).
idea_hypotheses.mechanism_lineage: M5 from `snapinvoice`, `brief-case-onboarding`, `pet-fairquote`. M6 from `fafsadecoder`, `payroll-picket`, `compass-rosetta`. M7 from `denialpilot` (insurance evidence packet) — the SNAP stolen-benefits claim is structurally identical to an insurance denial appeal: a 'state denied/replaced' decision + a 90-day appeal window + a printable evidence packet. M9 from `docket-guard`, `closing-clock`. M20 from `compass-rosetta` (B2B regulatory routing). M24 from `rental-turnover-ready-ack`, `pet-farewell-kit`. M25 (authority boundary) is the explicit differentiator from the $200-500 'EBT skimming protection' scam services that have proliferated since Dec 20 2024. idea_hypotheses.primary_risk: (1) The state EBT portal integration is fragile — Conduent / Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) run most state EBT systems and the consumer-side auth flow varies. idea_hypotheses.source_overlap_check: No name/one_liner collision with the off-limits list. synthesis_verdict: Three ideas advance: HoursLog (primary), SkimShield (secondary), PlatePath (tertiary). All three pass the mock-hackathon lens (RevenueCat-eligible B2C subscription, 6-week buildable from M5+M6+M9+M19+M24+M25 bundle, weekly-ritual + shareable, crafted subscription with caregiver/care-team tier). All three are B2C or B2C-flavoured and domain-separated from the off-limits list and the existing corpus records. HoursLog is the strongest single wedge — the OBBBA 55-64 expansion + the Nov 2 2025 state-waiver auto-termination + the existing 33-state redetermination backlog + the 90-day fair-hearing window all converge in 14 months to make 'consumer-side SNAP ABAWD 80-hour documentation' a real 2026 wedge; the M25 authority-boundary label is the explicit guardrail vs the $200-500 'SNAP application help' scam. SkimShield is the highest-stakes wedge — the federal replacement expiration Dec 20 2024 + the $555M projected FY2025-FY2026 fraud + only 2 states with replacement programs = a real consumer-side gap; the M7+M9+M20+M24+M25 bundle is the same mechanism family as the corpus's regulated-handoff cluster, but applied to a benefit that was structurally never protected the way credit/debit cards were. PlatePath is the broadest TAM — 38M Medicare discharges/yr, ~30-50% non-compliance with discharge dietary instructions, 78M baby boomers aging into the caregiver-for-parent cohort, the food-inflation wave making the 20% non-SNAP portion grow faster than inflation; the M19 multi-form-synthesis (discharge summary + med list + per-store inventory + SNAP eligibility) is a genuinely new vertical narrow of the mechanism. Primary risk across all three: state/federal regulator action (Ohio/California/Texas JFS shipping a state-side recertification pre-fill, Maryland/CA scaling the stolen-benefits auto-file to all 50 states, CMS publishing a federal post-discharge nutrition tool); secondary risk: a major platform (Walmart, Kroger, Amazon) shipping the consumer-side layer of any of these before a 6-week hackathon can validate. Recommend advancing all three to the corpus and parking the SNAP-online / WIC-remote-cert / shrinkflation / Dollar General / restaurant-letter-grade / MTM / PRx wedges for future ticks. The HoursLog → SkimShield → PlatePath trio is the 'consumer-side regulatory unlock' family (parallel to MCADetector → QuarterNest → ClosingClock in tick 20 for SMB), and the next 2-3 ticks should focus on whether the family can be extended to the WIC 21st Century WIC Act + SNAP online + Dollar General wedges.
